Due to health recommendations from the Center for Disease Control and State of California
Division of Occupational Safety and Health (Cal/OSHA), and the declared state of emergency
wherein social distancing measures have been imposed or recommended, the CITY OF
AVALON’S CITY COUNCIL and PLANNING COMMISSION MEETINGS SHALL GENERALLY
BE AVAILABLE TO THE PUBLIC REMOTELY. The general public may attend the meeting in
the Council Chambers however must adhere to social distancing requirements. The public is
encouraged to watch and participate from the safety of their homes while practicing social
distancing.

Council Chambers are open to a maximum 30 members of the general public. Once the Council
Chambers reach maximum occupancy, the general public may participate in Oral
Communication and address the City Council on an agenda item in person by waiting in the City
Hall Court Yard and entering the Chambers one at a time at the appropriate time. No one will be
admiffed into the Council Chambers who is ill or exhibiting symptoms of COVID-1 9. Additionally,

agenda items by providing Comments via Zoom or by sending comments to

CONSENT CALENDAR

1.  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote Teleconference/Virtual City Council Meetings
  Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361
  At the November 16, 2021 City Council meeting, the City Council made findings pursuant
  to Assembly Bill 361 to continue to meet remotely. To continue this practice, it is required,
  that the City Council determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the
  Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
  to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or
  recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and
  that as a result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent
  risks to the health or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every
  thirty (30) days, the City Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming October
  4, 2022 meeting and thirty (30) days thereafter.

  Recommended Action
  Determine that the COVID-1 9 state of emergency proclaimed by the Governor still exists
  and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue to have
  teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
  measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result
  of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the
  health or safety of attendees.

2.  Procurement of Two (2) Yamaha Outboard Engines
  On October 21, 2021, the City of was awarded $40,000 in grant funding from the
  Department of Parks and Recreation, Division of Boating and Waterways (DBW) for the
  purchase two Yamaha outboard engines. The funding will replace two aging outboard
  engines currently in use by the Avalon Harbor Department.
  Recommended Action
  Authorize the Harbor Master to purchase two (2) Yamaha outboard engines for a not to
  exceed sum of $40,000.

3.  Ratify Prior Action Replenishment of Infill for Joe Machado Field
  -

  The City contracted Hellas Construction, Inc. to design, build and install a synthetic turf
  at Joe Machado Field. Within the warranty offered by Hellas it is mandated that the City
  adheres to a minimum maintenance schedule, including annual refill and regular tilling of
  the infill on the field.
  Recommended Action
  Determine that an emergency existed and ratify action by the City Manager and
  Community Services Supervisor to undertake necessary maintenance to replenish infill
  at Joe Machado Field. Authorize a Fiscal Year 2022-23 budget amendment allocating an
  additional $34,500 to fund 10265-5644.

4.  Award Green Pleasure Pier 2022 Repair Proect
  Since 2018, City Staff has been working on a long term maintenance plan for the Green
  Pleasure Pier. Currently maintenance work on the pier is accomplished by City forces
  where feasible, but there is a limit to the size and scope of a project. When the size and
  scope becomes too large a contractor is necessary. The first project that needs to be
  completed this fall is the repair of five piles.
  Recommended Action
  (1) Award the construction contract for the Green Pleasure Pier 2022 Repair Project to
  Jilk Heavy Construction, Inc. for a not to exceed amount of $266,980.00 (2) Approve a
  supplemental appropriation of $100,000 to the current budget of $225,000.00 for a total
  project budget in FY 2022-23 of $325,000.00.

   CITY OF AVALON CITY COUNCIL

MEETING DATE:  September 13, 2022  AGENDA ITEM:  I
ORIGINATING DEP:  City Attorney  CITY MANAGER:

PREPARED BY:  Scott Campbell, City Attorney

SUBJECT:  Findings to Continue to Hold Remote TeleconferenceNirtual City
  Council Meetings Pursuant to Assembly Bill 361

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that the COVID-19 state of emergency proclaimed
by the Governor still exists and has been considered by the City Council in deciding to continue
to have teleconference meetings and that state or local officials have imposed or recommended
measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, and that as a result of the
COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health or safety
of attendees.

REPORT SUMMARY: Traditionally, the Brown Act allows for teleconference or virtual meetings,
provided that the physical locations of the legislative body’s members joining by teleconference
are posted on the agenda, that those locations are open to the public and that a quorum of the
members is located within its jurisdiction. Newly enacted AB 361 provides an exception to these
procedures in order to allow for fully virtual meetings during proclaimed emergencies, including
the COVID-19 pandemic.

Since March of 2020 and the issuance of Governor Newsom’s Executive Order N-29-20, which
suspended portions of the Brown Act relating to teleconferencing, the City Council has had virtual
meetings without having to post the location of the legislative body members attending virtually.
Most public agencies have been holding public meetings using virtual platforms since this time.
In June of 2021, Governor Newsom issued Executive Order N-08-21, which provided that the
exceptions contained in EO N-29-20 would sunset on September 30, 2021.

On September 10, 2021, the Legislature adopted AB 361, which allows public agencies to hold
fully virtual meetings under certain circumstances without the posting of the agenda from each
location a legislative body member is attending. Governor Newsom signed the bill into law on
September 16, 2021. Because it contained an urgency provision, it took immediate effect.

SpecIfic Findings Required underAB 361

Under AS 361, the City Council can hold virtual meetings without providing notice of the City
Council’s teleconference location if the City Council makes the determination that there is a
Governor-proclaimed state of emergency, which the City Council will consider in their
determination, and one of two secondary criteria listed below exists:

  1. State or local officials have imposed or recommended measures to promote social
  distancing in connection with COVID-19; or

6509.00034520811
   2. The City Council determines that requiring a meeting in person would present an
  imminent risk to the health or safety of attendees.

COVID-19 continues to present an imminent threat to the health or safety of members of the
public, and the Governor’s declaration of a COVID-19 emergency still exists. Although vaccines
are now widely available, many people in the State and County are still not fully vaccinated and
remain susceptible to infection. The disease can still spread rapidly through person-to-person
contact and those in close proximity. Further, more contagious variants of the disease are now
present in the State and County, the most predominant of which is a new variant of the Omnicron
variant. The County of Los Angeles recently re-instituted some mandates given the rise in cases
and deaths nationally and public health officials have indicated that they may reinstitute certain
mask requirements if cases continue to rise. The City’s economy is dependent upon visitors to
the island, the presence of which, increases the likelihood of transmission of the disease. Also,
having members of the public attend council meetings at locations where council members are
in attendance due to their desire to avoid exposure to COVID-19 poses an imminent risk to the
health or safety of attendees.

Re-Authorization is Required Within 30 Days

The City Council made the findings listed above at its August 16, 2022 City Council meeting.
Consistent with the provisions of Government Code Section 54953(e), the findings must be made
every 30 days “after teleconferencing for the first time’ under AR 361. Thus, if the City Council
desires to continue to meet remotely without having to post the location of each teleconference
location, the City Council must again find that the COVID-19 emergency still exists and that one
of the two following findings can be made: that state or local officials have imposed or
recommended measures to promote social distancing in connection with COVID-19, or, that a
result of the COVID-19 emergency, meeting in person would present imminent risks to the health
or safety of attendees. Because these findings must be made every thirty (30) days, the City
Council will have to make these findings at its upcoming October 4, 2022 meeting and thirty (30)
days thereafter.

It is recommended that the City Council make these findings.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City Council will
have to follow the Brown Act provisions that existed prior to the COVID-19 pandemic.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: That the City Council make the findings under AB 361 at its October 4,
2022 City Council meeting.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: N/A

FISCAL IMPACTS: None.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.

ATTACHMENTS: None.

SUBJECT:  Procurement of Two (2) Yamaha Outboard Engines

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Authorize the Harbor Master to purchase two (2) Yamaha
outboard engines for a not to exceed sum of $40,000.

REPORT SUMMARY: On Dctober 21, 2021, the City of was awarded $40,000 in grant funding
from the Department of Parks and Recreation: Division of Boating and Waterways (DBW) for
the purchase two Yamaha outboard engines. The funding will replace two aging outboard
engines currently in use by the Avalon Harbor Department.

The Harbor Department solicited quotes from qualified three vendors per the City’s
procurement policy Avalon Boat Stand: Ryan Boats! and West Coast Marine Service.
  —

Avalon Boat Stand! and Ryan Boats declined to provide estimates stating issues with the supply
chain were causing delays for obtaining outboard engines.

West Coast Marine Services has responded and provided an estimate totaling $37777.15;
however, West Coast Marine Services could not provide a timeline for delivery of the two
outboard engines.

The Harbor Master has been in contact with DBW Staff regarding supply chain delays and the
difficulty in procuring quotes. DBW Staff directed the City to proceed with the purchase
according to the grant and City procurement policies.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Patrol Boat Engines are budgeted within the FY 2022-23 Capital
Improvement Budget Project Number 207007, Account Number 10470-6889.
  -

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: Grant funding may be
revoked if the purchase is not made per the funding agreement.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: Pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Ratify Prior Action  -  Replenishment of InfilI for Joe Machado Field

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): Determine that an emergency existed and ratify action by the
City Manager and Community Services Supervisor to undertake necessary maintenance to
replenish infill at Joe Machado Field. Authorize a fiscal year 2022-23 budget amendment
allocating an additional $34,500 to fund 10265-5644.

REPORT SUMMARY: The City of Avalon contracted Hellas Construction, Inc. (Hellas) in 2016
to design, build and install a synthetic turf at Joe Machado Field. The products and work
offered by Hellas came with an 8-year manufacturer’s warranty. Within the warranty it is
mandated that the City adheres to a minimum maintenance schedule, including annual refill
and regular tilling of the infill on the field.

Due to Staffing and other resource and funding limitations associated with the COVID-19
  —

pandemic and emergency budget reductions regular maintenance of the field was deferred.
  —

The deferred maintenance, drought conditions and sudden increased use has resulted in
migration of the infill in high use areas goal mouth, penalty kick, and high slide areas.
  —

Though migration in high use areas is more significant than other areas, the entire field needs
infill replacement/replenishment. An assessment from Hellas determined approximately 20
Supersacks of infill are required. Due to the nature of our warranty, Hellas contractors will be
needed to perform the work.

On August 29, 2022, City Staff received a quote from Hellas of $54,500.00 for labor and
materials. Hellas informed City Staff that materials used for infill were heavily impacted by the
ongoing global supply chain issues, and indicated time was of the essence in authorizing the
work to be completed.

Failure to add infill may result in degradation of the field and potential significant damage to
this piece of community infrastructure, and/or may create public safety hazards. As the City’s
only athletic field available for high school as well as community use, Joe Machado Field is in
constant demand.

Title 3, Chapter 3-4.111 of the Avalon Municipal Code authorizes the City Manager to procure
services or supplies without immediate City Council approval. The City Manager determined

6509.000290408.1
 expedited replacement of the infill constituted an emergent situation and authorized
acceptance of the proposal provided by Hellas,

Approximately $20,000 is allocated in Fiscal Year 2022-23 to fund 10265-5644, an additional
$34,500 needs to be added to the budget.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure maintenance and public safety.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Fiscal Year Budget 2022-23 fund 10265-5644 has $20,000 is allocated.
An additional $34500 needs to be added to the budget.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The City may be out
of compliance with warranty for Joe Machado Field and potential infrastructure failure may
occur if it is not properly maintained.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Implement City Council direction.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT:  Pursuant to the Brown Act.

SUBJECT:  Award Green Pleasure Pier 2022 Repair Project

RECOMMENDED ACTION(S): (1) Award the construction contract for the Green Pleasure Pier
2022 Repair Project to Jilk Heavy Construction, Inc. for a not to exceed amount of $266,980.00
(2) Approve a supplemental appropriation of $100,000 to the current budget of $225,000.00 for
a total project budget in FY 2022-23 of $325,000.00.

REPORT SUMMARY: Since 2018, City Staff has been working on a long term maintenance
plan for the Green Pleasure Pier. Currently maintenance work on the pier is accomplished by
City forces where feasible, but there is a limit to the size and scope of a project. When the size
and scope becomes too large a contractor is necessary. Based on the City’s procurement
standards this requires a competitive bid. Additionally, with a larger scope project that enters the
water, an array of permits are required in addition to the development of contract documents
such as plans and specifications. Early on in this process it was determined that the development
of the contract documents, permitting documents and procurement would become a significant
cost for each time the City developed a new project. Based on this fact, City Staff began
developing a programmatic approach to delivering a multi-year heavy maintenance contract for
a period of five years. The intent would be a project that could provide a heavy pier maintenance
contract every one to two years that was procured from one design and permitting package, but
delivered by priority of work items when funds become available. The contract documents and
permits that are being created for this singular repair activity are also being utilized to facilitate
the programmatic long term program. The intent would be to come into agreement with the
permit agencies for a five-year permit as well as to competitively bid the work with a five-year
term contract.

The first project that needs to be completed this fall is the repair of five piles. Each of these five.
piles are in poor shape and must be completed in the near term as they are either missing or
have very little structural integrity remaining. Included with this bid solicitation was an additive
alternate for pier condition assessment above and below the waterline. This additive alternate
item is able to be added to the base bid. This item will assist in the preparation for the long term
maintenance contract and is efficient since we will be having divers in the water with the current
work. A bid solicitation was published on April 18, 2022. Three contractors showed interest with
two eventually submitting a proposal. The bid solicitation was protracted due to many contractor
questions and clarifications, but that process helps the contractor and the City to have a better
understanding of the work and the effort to deliver the construction before the contract is written.
The two bids were received and opened on August 10, 2022. Jilk Heavy Construction, Inc. was
 the low bidder with a base bid of $239,450.00 and an additive alternate of $27,530.00 for total
of $266,980.00. The second bidder was Connolly-Pacific Co with a base bid of $363,895.00
and an additive alternate of $33,140.00 for total of $397,035.00. Bids were evaluated for
completeness and adhering to the solicitation requirements. Both were deemed complete and
responsive. Based on low bid for the base bid, and value for the additive alternate, Staff
recommends that Jilk Heavy Construction, Inc. be awarded the base bid and the additive
alternate for a total of $266,980.00.

The recommended construction bid is greater than the current remaining approved project
budget of $210,880.00. Therefore, Staff is recommending a supplemental appropriation for
$100,000 from the Harbor Reserve Fund. This will allow the construction project to commence
as well as continuing the permitting and design effort for the programmatic multi-year to be
completed this fiscal year.

GOAL ALIGNMENT: Infrastructure reliability and safety.

FISCAL IMPACTS: Additional cost of $100,000 funded from Harbor Reserve Fund.

CONSEQUENCES OF NOT FOLLOWING RECOMMENDED ACTION: The necessary repairs
to the Green Pleasure Pier would be delayed.

FOLLOW UP ACTION: Execute procurement contract.

ADVERTISING, NOTICE AND PUBLIC CONTACT: This item was properly listed on the posted
agenda pursuant to the Brown Act.
